articles.title: Vagas de emprego no Amazonas: IBGE, Coca-Cola e Sine têm mil vagas | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre as oportunidades, estão 829 vagas temporárias para recenseador do IBGE, 94 vagas na Solar Coca-Cola, 32 na Eneva e 140 oportunidades divulgadas pelo Sine Amazonas para esta sexta-feira (13).
articles.summary: Há oportunidades para níveis fundamental e médio no IBGE, Solar Coca-Cola, Eneva e Sine Amazonas, com salários atrativos e benefícios em diversos municípios do estado.
articles.body:
Carteira de trabalho — Foto: Marcello Casal Jr/Agência Brasil

O Amazonas tem mais de mil oportunidades de emprego abertas em empresas privadas e em órgãos públicos. As vagas são oferecidas pela Eneva, Solar Coca-Cola, Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) e pelo Sine Amazonas, com opções para diferentes níveis de escolaridade e áreas de atuação.

Entre as oportunidades, estão 829 vagas temporárias para recenseador do IBGE , 94 vagas na Solar Coca-Cola , 32 na Eneva e 140 oportunidades divulgadas pelo Sine Amazonas para esta sexta-feira (13).

Há vagas para profissionais das áreas de indústria, comércio, logística, construção civil, manutenção, administração e vendas. Algumas oportunidades também aceitam candidatos sem experiência e pessoas em busca do primeiro emprego.

Confira abaixo os detalhes de cada seleção e saiba como participar:

IBGE oferece 829 vagas temporárias no Amazonas

O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) oferece 829 vagas temporárias para recenseador no Amazonas. Os profissionais vão trabalhar no 12º Censo Agropecuário, Florestal e Aquícola, com visitas a propriedades rurais e coleta de informações sobre a produção no estado.

As inscrições seguem até as 23h59 do dia 25 de novembro de 2026, pelo site da Fundação Cesgranrio . Para participar, é necessário ter ensino fundamental completo.

O salário fixo é de R$ 1.741, mas a remuneração pode chegar a R$ 4.370 por mês, conforme a produtividade. Os contratados também terão direito a auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192, auxílio pré-escolar, 13º salário proporcional, férias proporcionais acrescidas de um terço e auxílio para deslocamento.

As oportunidades estão distribuídas por diferentes municípios do estado, incluindo Careiro , Itacoatiara , Manacapuru , Manaus , Autazes , São Gabriel da Cachoeira e Tefé .

A prova objetiva está prevista para 31 de janeiro de 2027. A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 70.

A Solar Coca-Cola abriu 94 vagas de emprego no Amazonas. Desse total, 22 são temporárias e fazem parte do Plano Verão, programa que reforça as equipes durante o período de maior consumo de bebidas e as festas de fim de ano.

As contratações temporárias ocorrem entre outubro e dezembro, com contratos de 30 a 120 dias. Outras 72 oportunidades são efetivas, com previsão de entrada dos novos funcionários até janeiro.

Entre os cargos disponíveis estão promotor de vendas e auxiliar de expedição, além de funções nas áreas de logística e transporte.

A maioria das vagas exige ensino médio completo, mas também há oportunidades para quem concluiu o ensino fundamental. Algumas funções exigem Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH), experiência profissional ou cursos específicos.

A empresa oferece benefícios como vale-transporte, cesta básica, plano de saúde e vale-refeição.

Os interessados podem consultar os requisitos e realizar a inscrição pelo site de recrutamento da Solar Coca-Cola .

A Eneva está com 32 vagas abertas para trabalhar no Complexo Azulão, em Silves, no interior do Amazonas.

As oportunidades abrangem diferentes áreas, como operação, manutenção, segurança do trabalho, laboratório e administração.

Entre os cargos disponíveis estão operador de planta, técnico de manutenção mecânica, técnico químico, técnico de segurança do trabalho, técnico de instrumentação e analista administrativo.

As oportunidades fazem parte da ampliação das atividades da companhia no município. A empresa também busca fortalecer a contratação de trabalhadores amazonenses.

Os requisitos, as etapas da seleção e as informações sobre cada função estão disponíveis no portal de recrutamento da Eneva .

Sine Amazonas divulga 140 vagas para sexta-feira (13)

O Sine Amazonas está com 140 vagas de emprego abertas para esta sexta-feira (13). As oportunidades abrangem áreas como logística, comércio, construção civil, indústria, alimentação, manutenção e serviços gerais.

Entre os cargos disponíveis estão operador logístico, auxiliar de cozinha, atendente de balcão, montador de móveis, pedreiro, servente de obras, auxiliar de produção, vendedor e mecânico diesel.

Há também oportunidades destinadas a pessoas com deficiência (PcD) e reabilitados do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS). Algumas vagas aceitam candidatos sem experiência e quem procura o primeiro emprego.

Os interessados devem comparecer à Casa do Trabalhador do Sine Amazonas, localizada na Galeria+, na Avenida Djalma Batista, nº 1.018, entre o Amazonas Shopping e o Manaus Plaza Shopping.

A distribuição de senhas e o atendimento serão realizados das 8h às 13h.

Para participar da seleção, é necessário apresentar:

Carteira de Trabalho e Previdência Social (CTPS);

Comprovante de vacinação contra a Covid-19.

Não é necessário levar cópias. Os documentos originais são suficientes.

Além da unidade central, os interessados podem procurar as agências do Sine Amazonas nos PACs Studio 5, Alvorada e Via Norte, no Shopping Cidade Leste e no SindMetal.

articles.title: Árvores Gigantes da Amazônia: Parque ganha nova base e trilha no PA | G1
articles.standfirst: Estruturas foram inauguradas em Almeirim e devem fortalecer a fiscalização, pesquisas científicas e o turismo sustentável em uma área que abriga a maior árvore da América Latina.
articles.summary: O Parque das Árvores Gigantes da Amazônia inaugurou base e trilha de 5 km para proteger o angelim-vermelho de 88 metros e fomentar o turismo sustentável no Pará.
articles.body:
Parque das Árvores Gigantes da Amazônia ganha base operacional e trilha de 5 km em Almeirim, no PA — Foto: Divulgação

O Parque Estadual Ambiental das Árvores Gigantes da Amazônia, localizado no município de Almeirim, no oeste do Pará, ganhou uma nova base operacional e uma trilha de aproximadamente 5 quilômetros. As estruturas foram inauguradas no dia 30 de outubro e devem ampliar as condições de fiscalização, pesquisa científica, monitoramento ambiental e visitação turística na unidade de conservação.

O parque abriga o angelim-vermelho, árvore com 88,5 metros de altura, considerada a maior já registrada na América Latina. A unidade de conservação foi criada em setembro de 2024 e protege cerca de 560 mil hectares de floresta.

As novas estruturas fazem parte do projeto Árvores Gigantes para uma Nova Era – Fase II, desenvolvido pela Fundação Amazônia Sustentável (FAS), em parceria com o Instituto de Desenvolvimento Florestal e da Biodiversidade do Estado do Pará (IDEFLOR-Bio), com financiamento do Andes Amazon Fund (AAF).

A construção da infraestrutura levou aproximadamente sete meses. O espaço conta com cozinha, banheiros, alojamentos, sistemas sustentáveis de energia e abastecimento de água, passarelas de acesso, porto e mirante para contemplação da floresta.

Antes da implantação da base, as expedições realizadas na região dependiam principalmente de acampamentos improvisados. Com a nova estrutura, pesquisadores, equipes de fiscalização e visitantes passam a contar com melhores condições de permanência no local.

A Trilha do Santuário das Árvores Gigantes também recebeu intervenções de manejo e sinalização. Ao longo dos cerca de 5 quilômetros, os visitantes poderão conhecer árvores gigantes, acessar um mirante de observação e visitar a cachoeira do Jacaré. As intervenções foram planejadas para orientar o percurso e reduzir os impactos sobre a vegetação e o solo.

Segundo Juliane Menezes, coordenadora executiva do projeto pela FAS, a infraestrutura é importante para consolidar a gestão da unidade de conservação e ampliar as ações de proteção ambiental.

O gerente do IDEFLOR-Bio, Júlio César Meyer Júnior, também destacou que a trilha poderá facilitar o acesso de pesquisadores e visitantes à floresta.

Árvores gigantes em Almeirim, no Pará — Foto: Divulgação

A inauguração foi marcada por uma expedição que reuniu pesquisadores, representantes de instituições públicas e equipes técnicas. O acesso ao parque exigiu uma operação que combinou transporte aéreo, terrestre e aproximadamente 190 quilômetros de navegação pelo Rio Jari.

O percurso inclui corredeiras e cachoeiras e foi realizado durante o período de seca, condição que dificultou a navegação. O transporte de materiais para a construção das estruturas também exigiu planejamento e adaptações devido à distância e às características da região.

Aldemir Pereira da Cunha, um dos quatro pilotos responsáveis pelo transporte fluvial durante a expedição, explicou que a navegação pelo Rio Jari exige conhecimento das mudanças no nível das águas ao longo do ano.

Segundo ele, os pilotos precisam conhecer os diferentes trajetos para garantir a segurança dos passageiros e das embarcações.

Durante a expedição, pesquisadores também identificaram uma árvore gigante com altura estimada em 75 metros, nas proximidades da nova trilha.

O professor e pesquisador do Instituto Federal do Amapá (IFAP), Diego Armando Silva da Silva, explicou que a floresta abriga árvores que podem ter entre 400 e 600 anos de idade.

Turismo pode gerar renda para comunidades

Além da conservação ambiental e da pesquisa científica, a nova infraestrutura busca ampliar o potencial do turismo de natureza na região do Vale do Jari.

A expectativa é que moradores de comunidades locais possam participar de atividades relacionadas à visitação, como transporte fluvial, condução de turistas e prestação de serviços.

Para o secretário municipal de Turismo de Laranjal do Jari, Jairo Cleiton dos Santos Silva, a estrutura pode ampliar as oportunidades de emprego e renda na região, a partir da valorização das árvores gigantes e das paisagens naturais.

Parque protege cerca de 560 mil hectares

Criado em setembro de 2024, o Parque Estadual Ambiental das Árvores Gigantes da Amazônia protege aproximadamente 560 mil hectares de floresta no município de Almeirim, no Pará.

Entre os principais patrimônios naturais da unidade está um exemplar de angelim-vermelho (Dinizia excelsa), com 88,5 metros de altura e aproximadamente 400 anos de idade.

Expedições científicas realizadas na região também identificaram dezenas de outras árvores gigantes, tornando o território uma área de interesse para pesquisas sobre a biodiversidade amazônica.

O projeto Árvores Gigantes para uma Nova Era – Fase II tem como objetivo consolidar a gestão do parque por meio da implantação de infraestrutura, elaboração de plano de gestão, incentivo à pesquisa científica e desenvolvimento do turismo sustentável.

articles.summary: No mesmo dia, o maior complexo portuário da América Latina foi alvo de um ataque hacker e uma invasão aos sistemas da Caixa Vida e Previdência expôs dados de milhões de brasileiros.
articles.body:
Na sexta-feira passada (6), o maior complexo portuário da América Latina, o Porto de Santos, foi alvo de um ataque hacker. No mesmo dia, uma invasão aos sistemas da Caixa Vida e Previdência expôs dados de milhões de brasileiros. Os dois casos não são episódios isolados: diversos ataques foram registrados na Europa nas últimas semanas. Na França, por exemplo, mais de 500 supermercados foram invadidos, assim como uma empresa que presta serviços de banco de sangue para o governo francês. No sistema financeiro, a maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo sofreu um roubo da ordem de R$ 6 bilhões em ativos digitais. Especialistas apontam que as ferramentas de IA estão por trás dessa epidemia de investidas contra a segurança cibernética.

Neste episódio, Victor Boyadjian recebe dois convidados. Primeiro, ele conversa com o jornalista Bruno Natal para explicar essa onda de ataques recentes. Depois, Victor entrevista Thiago Diogo, pesquisador de cibersegurança, sobre os riscos para a economia global e para a segurança de Estados nacionais, como o Brasil.

Convidados: Bruno Natal, jornalista, documentarista e apresentador do podcast Resumido, e Thiago Diogo, pesquisador de cibersegurança e fundador da Duranium, consultoria especializada em segurança e inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Police officers sacked for recording vulnerable people while on duty
articles.summary: The behaviour of the two male officers is branded "utterly despicable" by the police ombudsman.
articles.body:
Two male Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) officers have been sacked for taking videos and photos of 18 vulnerable people they had been sent to help.

In one video, a woman with learning difficulties was filmed in bed and asked about her sex life.

The two officers, identified as Officers A and B, had been tasked to her house in 2021 after a report of concern for her safety.

Police Ombudsman Jacqui Durkin said their behaviour had been "utterly despicable".

Some of the videos and pictures taken by the officers were shared on WhatsApp, including with a member of the public, and contained "sexualised, derogatory and demeaning commentary".

Their actions came to light during an investigation into Officer A, who was accused of having a relationship with a woman he met during the course of his duties.

His home and workplace were searched and electronic devices were seized for examination.

He was found to have taken videos and pictures of people who had requested assistance, reported crimes, were intoxicated or considered at risk of self-harm.

Some were filmed in people's homes, others in hospitals and in police vehicles.

They spanned a period between 2016 and 2021.

Five videos found on Officer A's phone featured an elderly and apparently vulnerable man, filmed in his home and on a street from a police car.

They show the poor state of his living conditions and included the officer making mocking comments about his sex life.

Two other videos were recorded of women who had been involved in a neighbour dispute, one of whom was intoxicated.

Officer B took photos of two vulnerable women, which he shared with Officer A, along with messages which referred to the women in derogatory terms.

Durkin said: "Almost all of the people affected by these actions were vulnerable, some extremely so.

"These now former officers showed no respect for people's privacy or dignity at their time of need and seriously undermined their trust and confidence in policing.

"One also shared a series of messages with a member of the public, showing scant regard for the confidentiality of police enquiries.

"They were unworthy of the role of police officer and it is only right that they have been dismissed from the PSNI."

The ombudsman submitted files to the Public Prosecution Service (PPS) in relation to the images, videos and messages found on Officer A's phones.

The files concerned potential misconduct in public office by Officer A and potential data protection offences by both Officer A and Officer B.

The PPS directed that neither should be prosecuted.

However, it noted that offences under the Communications Act would have been relevant if they had not already been statute barred before the ombudsman discovered the material.

In a statement, the PPS said that the decision not to prosecute was made on the basis "there was insufficient evidence to provide a reasonable prospect of conviction".

It said that proceedings for data protection offences were "already statute barred" due to how much time had elapsed between the alleged offences and the PPS receiving the files.

The PPS said that while prosecutions were not pursued, this "does not diminish the gravity of the professional misconduct identified".

"We would encourage anyone who has experienced criminal or professional misconduct to report their concerns," it added.

Deputy Chief Constable Bobby Singleton described the officers' conduct as "horrifying".

He added: "The behaviour described by the ombudsman falls far below the standards the public is entitled to expect from police officers.

"It represented a serious breach of trust, particularly affecting people who were entitled to care, compassion and professional support at times of acute vulnerability."

Singleton said all cases of misconduct are taken "extremely seriously" and this was reflected "in the dismissals of two officers".

"We are sorry that individuals who sought the assistance of police were let down in this way," he added

Policing Board vice-chair Mukesh Sharma described the officers' conduct as "shameful and disgusting".

He added: "These officers showed a callous disregard to people at their most vulnerable and breached the trust placed in them from those seeking help.

"Their actions are the antithesis of the professionalism that we rightly expect from police officers serving the community."

One other officer, known as Officer C, was given a final written warning.

A fourth officer, Officer D, faced no action - they had been present when Officer A had recorded a video but stated they had been unaware of the recording.

The justice minister said she was "deeply saddened at the behaviours outlined" in the report.

Naomi Long condemned the actions of the officers, describing it as "abhorrent, wholly unacceptable and completely indefensible".

"There is no place in our police service for officers who behave in this way."

Long also said it "does not represent the bravery, decency and compassion that the majority of police officers display in their jobs".

articles.title: CEO of world's largest AI models repository, Hugging Face, calls Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO 'sad'; says: I want to make one thing clear that we will keep fighting for ...
articles.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue expressed dismay following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, moving quickly to reassure the open-source
articles.body: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue expressed dismay following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, moving quickly to reassure the open-source artificial intelligence community that his company’s mission remains unchanged ahead of its pending multibillion-dollar acquisition by the chipmaker. For those unaware, Hugging Face is the world's biggest repository for AI models.In a post on the social platform X, formerly Twitter, Delangue called the leadership change at Nvidia a “really sad day” while vowing to maintain momentum for open-source development. He wrote, “This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!”Delangue’s remarks are seen as the worry among open-source advocates regarding Nvidia’s future commitment to the ecosystem without Huang at the helm. In September, Nvidia announced plans to acquire Hugging Face -- a central hub for open-source AI models -- for $12.9 billion. The transaction represents the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history, trailing only its $20 billion purchase of chipmaker Groq’s assets in December 2025.The acquisition, which remains scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, has already drawn regulatory scrutiny. In October, Reuters reported that the U.S. Department of Justice had begun inquiring into how the merger might affect competition in the AI sector. Although Nvidia pledged to maintain Hugging Face’s open support, critics and regulators have noted that the deal would give the hardware giant control over a primary distribution channel for AI models.Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia had positioned itself as a vocal champion of open-source and open-weight models—systems whose underlying parameters are publicly accessible. During his keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas in January this year, Huang remarked that open-source models had “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.”In July, Huang used his first-ever post on X to publish an AI policy letter signed by 25 technology companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, and Hugging Face. The letter urged the U.S. government to avoid over-regulating open-weight models, arguing that software anyone can “download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” prevents vendor lock-in and makes AI more accessible.Huang wrote, "For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models."Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.

articles.title: 'What difference does it make?': Molester asked Mumbai woman before pushing her off platform; how Naigaon horror unfolded inside local train
articles.summary: VASAI: “What difference does it make?” was the response a 53-year-old man allegedly gave a 20-year-old woman when she confronted him for molesting her
articles.body: VASAI: “What difference does it make?” was the response a 53-year-old man allegedly gave a 20-year-old woman when she confronted him for molesting her inside a Mumbai local train.The exchange soon escalated into a physical altercation at Naigaon station, where the man allegedly pushed her onto the tracks. As she tried to climb back onto the platform, the train began moving, crushing her left arm below the elbow.The woman, who got married just five months ago, had gone to Malad on November 4 to buy a phone. With trains packed, she travelled to Borivli and boarded a Virar-bound slow local. She mistakenly entered the compartment reserved for persons with disabilities.According to her complaint, a man later identified as Jitendra Hirmukhe (53) repeatedly pushed against her inside the crowded compartment. Initially, she ignored him, but when the train reached Bhayander, he allegedly began touching her inappropriately.Both got off at Naigaon station around 7.15pm, where the woman confronted Hirmukhe. Instead of backing off, he allegedly touched her inappropriately again and asked her, “What difference does it make?”Angered by his response, the woman took off her slipper and threw it at him. Hirmukhe allegedly abused her, removed his own slipper and hit her with it.The train was still standing at the platform, and several passengers gathered as the confrontation escalated. Hirmukhe allegedly pushed the woman, causing her to fall onto the tracks into the gap between two coaches.As she tried to climb back onto the platform, the train started moving. She fell into the platform gap, and her left arm came under the train's wheels. The arm was severed below the elbow.Hirmukhe fled the spot. The woman was initially taken to a hospital in Vasai and later shifted to a Mumbai hospital for further treatment. She is undergoing treatment at a civic hospital.Bhayander railway police examined CCTV footage from the station and traced Hirmukhe to his residence in Wakipada, Naigaon East. He was arrested on November 9, five days after the incident. He originally hails from Dharashiv district.“He has stomach cancer and was travelling in the compartment reserved for persons with disabilities. We traced him with the help of CCTV footage and arrested him from Naigaon,” said Ganpat Tumbada, senior inspector, Bhayander railway police.Police initially registered a case under sections 74 (molestation), 117(2) (voluntarily causing hurt) and 352 (intentional insult) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Section 109 (attempt to murder) was subsequently added. Hirmukhe is in judicial custody.The woman has demanded the strictest punishment for the accused. “Despite having done nothing wrong, I had to go through this ordeal. articles.title: Trump moots toppling Cuba authorities before leaving office
articles.summary: Calling Cuba a failed nation, the US president hints at attack on the country before his term ends.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has said he would “certainly consider” using military force against Cuba, adding that he wants to “get Cuba done” before he leaves office in 2029.

In a phone interview on Thursday with conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt, of Salem News Channel, Trump was asked whether he was considering “freeing Cuba” through a military intervention.

“I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” he said, adding that the administration was “watching it very closely”.

Trump called the island “essentially a failed … place, nation, whatever you wanna call it”.

Politico reported that it was the first time Trump had put a timeline on a possible operation.

Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose parents are from Cuba, “would love to do it”.

“I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump said. He added that he won the Cuban vote in Florida by a wide margin.

Trump has repeatedly threatened to topple authorities in Cuba.

On Monday, he said Cuba “will fall fairly soon” and that the US would help it “on a humanitarian basis”.

In March, he said he believed he would have “the honour of taking Cuba”, making the remarks as the island’s power grid collapsed .

Trump put Cuba under a de facto oil blockade in January, after the US seized Venezuela’s president, Nicolas Maduro, and cut off Venezuelan oil to the island.

He signed an executive order declaring Cuba an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to the US and threatened tariffs on any country that supplied it with fuel.

The blockade has caused repeated nationwide blackouts, fuel and food shortages, and a humanitarian crisis.

Cuban officials have called it “collective punishment”.

Washington has added sanctions, including on Cuba’s state oil company, President Miguel Diaz-Canel and relatives of former President Raul Castro, and announced a new round this month targeting 10 people and entities tied to the government, military and oil industry.

The US has also issued an arrest warrant for Castro. Officials from both sides have held talks on the blockade, but Cuba’s foreign minister said in June there had been “no progress”.

In March, the head of US Southern Command told senators that US troops were not rehearsing for an invasion of Cuba.

Cuban officials said the island was ready for any attack.

articles.title: Spanish court suspends far-right group over alleged hate crimes
articles.summary: Judge orders office shut and accounts blocked after 14 arrests and the seizure of more than 20 firearms.
articles.body:
A Spanish judge has suspended the activities of the ultra-right group Nucleo Nacional as part of an investigation into alleged hate crimes and illegal association.

The court in the northern city of Gijon announced the ruling on Thursday, ordering the group’s office shut and its social media content and bank accounts blocked.

The move follows the arrest last week of 14 of its members on suspicion of inciting hatred against vulnerable groups and people with opposing ideologies.

The decision comes ahead of Spain’s general election on November 29 and a day after the first nationwide general strike in 14 years.

In a video posted on X, an unnamed Nucleo Nacional representative wearing a black shirt with the group’s logo said the movement was a victim of “persecution and political repression”.

Nucleo Nacional describes itself as a political movement. On its website, which has now been blocked and suspended by court order, it says it seeks a “national awakening”. Spanish authorities have scrutinised the group over its anti-immigration rhetoric, particularly after thousands of migrants crossed in July into Ceuta, Spain’s North African enclave.

Police also searched the group’s headquarters in Madrid and other locations. They said they seized more than 20 firearms, some of them unlicensed, along with large quantities of ammunition and other illegal weapons.

The court said key members of the organisation had already been placed under precautionary measures, including a ban on leaving Spain and a requirement to report weekly to a court.

Reuters also reported last month that Spanish police arrested three members of a far-right group in Madrid on October 3, after tens of thousands marched across the country over the housing crisis.

The Spanish government said far-right activists, some performing Nazi salutes, tried to reach demonstrators camped in the Puerta del Sol square.

articles.title: Indonesia’s vice president resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.summary: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesia’s vice president resigned on Thursday as questions grew over his eligibility for the office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials.
articles.body: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesia’s vice president resigned on Thursday as questions grew over his eligibility for the office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials. Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former popular President Joko Widodo, submitted his resignation to the leadership of the People’s Consultative Assembly, the country’s highest legislative body, at the parliament building in the capital, Jakarta. “There will always be political dynamics in public office, that’s normal,” his father, Widodo, told reporters from his hometown in Solo, adding that he had reminded his son that political positions are temporary. “We will continue to support President Prabowo’s government, especially programs that serve the interests of the broader public,” he said, referring to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The academic credentials investigation was apparently not related to investigations into allegations that top police officials had been involved in wiretapping targeting the president. Offers to resign to avoid further political turmoil Raka had offered to resign Tuesday during a meeting with Prabowo, saying he wanted to avoid a prolonged political controversy. He personally delivered his resignation letter to the president on Wednesday. Raka made no comment to reporters as he left the parliament building but released a video statement later Thursday, firmly rejecting suggestions that his resignation was linked to questions surrounding his educational background. “This was not an easy decision, but it was the best choice,” he said. “This is my personal decision and has nothing to do with my diploma. Once again, it has nothing to do with my diploma. All my educational documents are complete and have been submitted to the court.” Raka said his resignation should not be interpreted as an admission that he was unable to carry out his responsibilities. Instead, he described it as a major step intended to allow the government to move forward with greater focus and stability. Prabowo accepts Raka’s resignation Prabowo addressed the nation Thursday afternoon after holding a meeting with Raka and the parliamentary leadership at the presidential palace. Flanked by Raka and top leaders of parliament, a grim-looking Prabowo said that he accepted Raka’s resignation “with a heavy heart” and praised the vice president for showing “courage, responsibility and statesmanship” by stepping down. “He chose to resign for the greater interest of the nation, the state and the Indonesian people,” Prabowo said in a televised statement. “He has been a great help to me, from our election campaign through the past two years of government. Many of our achievements would not have been possible without his contribution.” Prabowo praised Raka’s dedication and hard work, highlighting Raka’s visits to 35 provinces and 149 regencies and cities to inspect 303 government projects during the past two years as examples of his commitment to public service. “I will continue to support him, and I pray that he and his family are given strength during what is undoubtedly a difficult time,” Prabowo said. Under the Indonesian Constitution, a vice presidential vacancy doesn’t trigger a new election. The office remains vacant until the People’s Consultative Assembly elects a replacement from two candidates nominated by the president within 60 days. Long-running allegations over candidacy lead to court disputes The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn’t meet election requirements. A subsequent petition, submitted Wednesday to the House leadership by 120 lawmakers from eight political parties, began a parliamentary process that could have led to his impeachment. The push for his impeachment was driven largely by long-running allegations that Raka’s candidacy was enabled by a Constitutional Court ruling that critics see as a conflict of interest and evidence of weak political accountability and dynastic privilege. Before Prabowo chose him as his running mate for the 2024 election, Raka didn’t meet the age requirement of 40 for vice presidential candidates. But the court’s contentious ruling in October 2023 carved an exception allowing those who served or had been elected as regional leaders to run at a younger age. Under Indonesian election law, a presidential or vice-presidential candidate must have completed senior high school or an equivalent level of education. Because Raka completed his secondary education overseas, he was required to provide documents showing that his qualifications were equivalent to an Indonesian high school diploma. Raka was the first vice president of the country to resign before the end of a term since the fall of dictator Suharto and the start of Indonesia’s democratic reforms in 1998. Parliamentary leaders were due to convene immediately to begin the process of selecting a replacement, Speaker Ahmad Muzani said. “We ask for the prayers and support of all Indonesians so that this democratic process can proceed smoothly and serve as a constructive new precedent in our constitutional system,” Muzani told reporters.

articles.title: Woman buys Rs 1,755 pressure cooker, finds rice and dal remain uncooked despite 3-4 whistles; consumer commission orders refund, Rs 12,000 compensation and Rs 3,000 costs, imposes Rs 21,000 penalty on store and dealer
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: A pressure cooker bought for Rs 1,755 was supposed to make everyday cooking easier.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: A pressure cooker bought for Rs 1,755 was supposed to make everyday cooking easier. Instead, a woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. When the same problem persisted while preparing dal the following day, she approached the seller for help. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755.The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost, along with compensation and litigation expenses, after finding deficiencies in the services provided by the three parties.The commission, presided over by Gudla Tanuja, with members Varri Krishna Murthy and Rahimunnisa Begum, passed the order on October 31. The woman had purchased a four-litre deep-pan pressure cooker from a store for Rs 1,755, paying through UPI. She said she first noticed the problem when she used it to cook rice on the day of purchase. Despite allowing the cooker to function for the prescribed three to four whistles, the rice was only partially cooked.An attempt to prepare dal the next day yielded the same result, according to her complaint. She then contacted the store, alleging that its staff responded insensitively and asked her to approach the company's service centre. However, citing her age and physical limitations, she said she could not visit the centre. The store subsequently collected the cooker from her and issued a service bill for its repair. But the woman maintained that she wanted a replacement rather than a repair. The company later informed her that it had instructed the dealer to replace the appliance, but the dealer had not acted on the instruction, the commission noted.The store and the dealer maintained that the cooker had been examined by service personnel, who had even shared a video demonstrating that it was working properly. Their lawyers told the commission that the woman had refused an offer to accompany her to the service centre for a demonstration. They also argued that she had insisted on a replacement despite the appliance being in working condition and was seeking an excessive amount as compensation.The store and dealer further contended that she had not submitted an expert opinion or technical report to establish a manufacturing defect. They also accused her of threatening litigation and claiming to have connections with consumer commission personnel. The manufacturer, meanwhile, argued that its warranty obligations were limited to repairing or replacing products with inherent manufacturing defects. It maintained that the cooker had undergone operational testing and was found to be functioning properly.The commission observed that the store, dealer and manufacturer had failed to produce the warranty terms before it. It also questioned their reliance on a proposed replacement as a goodwill gesture, asking why such an offer would have been made if the appliance had no problem. The bench held that the woman was entitled to a refund as a consumer exercising her legal rights under the Consumer Protection Act, and not merely because the company was willing to offer a goodwill replacement.It also took exception to the allegations that she had used purported connections within the commission to threaten the store and dealer. Describing the remarks as defamatory, the commission said they amounted to an attempt to tarnish the institution's image and included derogatory comments about the complainant.The commission directed the store, dealer and manufacturer to refund the Rs 1,755 paid for the cooker, pay Rs 12,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and bear Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs. articles.title: 'I may be jailed, they may try to kill me': Sheikh Hasina's defiant message on returning to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the threat of arrest, imprisonment or even death would not stop her from returning to Dhaka,
articles.body: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the threat of arrest, imprisonment or even death would not stop her from returning to Dhaka, asserting that she would rather die in her homeland than stay away from her people.In a rare audio interview with news agency IANS, Hasina said she was fully aware of the risks involved in returning to Bangladesh but maintained that fear had never stopped her from doing what she believed was right.“Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life. Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right,” the exiled leader stated.Expressing concern over the situation in Bangladesh, Hasina said the country was going through a difficult phase, alleging that Awami League leaders and workers were being persecuted while ordinary people were suffering and losing their homes and livelihoods.She said the hardships faced by the people had strengthened her determination to return and stand by them, irrespective of the consequences.“Today, my country is going through a terrible time. Our leaders and workers are being persecuted. Ordinary people are suffering, and families are losing their homes and livelihoods. How can I stay away while my people face such hardship? I have spent my entire political life with the people of Bangladesh. Whatever happens to me, I want to stand beside them. If I have to die, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina told IANS.Denies ordering killings during 2024 uprisingAddressing allegations over deaths during the 2024 uprising in Bangladesh, the former prime minister categorically denied ordering the killing of innocent people.Hasina accused the former Muhammad Yunus-led interim government of stopping a judicial inquiry she had initiated into the deaths and subsequently granting legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as “political resistance”.“Let me make one thing very clear. I never ordered the killing of innocent people. I reject that accusation completely. Every death was tragic. As Prime Minister, I had a responsibility to protect the lives of our citizens, and I wanted to know exactly what had happened. That is why, on July 18, 2024, I established a Judicial Enquiry Commission headed by a High Court judge. On August 1, I expanded it to a three-member commission so that every incident could be examined properly. But what happened after Muhammad Yunus assumed power? He stopped that investigation,” the former PM said.She questioned the interim administration's decision to halt the inquiry while pursuing murder cases against her and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers.“His administration subsequently granted legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as political resistance. At the same time, murder cases were brought against me and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers. If they really wanted the truth, why did they stop the judicial investigation that I had already established? Why should there be different standards of justice depending on someone's political identity?” she questioned.Rejects International Crimes Tribunal verdictHasina also rejected the proceedings of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) and the verdict against her, alleging that she was not given a genuine opportunity to defend herself.“As for the tribunal, I reject both the proceedings and the verdict. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as if the admin center is not available to you," read the post.Microsoft 365 outage impacts email, Teams, Copilot and other servicesMicrosoft 365 outage has affected Microsoft's email, workplace communication and cloud-based services. In its initial response to the outage, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of users experiencing problems accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods.The software company later identified elevated load across part of its infrastructure as a likely reason for the connectivity errors. It said several servers had become unexpectedly unavailable after failing automated health checks, shifting additional traffic onto the remaining infrastructure. In its update, Microsoft clarified that the elevated load was not being caused by an overall increase in traffic, but by the reduced availability of servers.Here’s what Microsoft said in its latest updateIn a latest udpate shared on X at 10:31am, Microsoft said that it is "engaged in multiple workstreams to alleviate impact, address our current blocker, and returning portions of service infrastructure back to a healthy state. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as if the admin center is not available to you".Microsoft 365 outage: Federal government departments impactedDue to the ongoing outage, several federal agencies have issued notices saying they are not receiving communications due to the outage. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) published this statement on its website: “Due to the global Microsoft outage, all urgent sanctions enquiries should be directed to the Australian Sanctions Office by telephone”.“As of Friday 13 November 2026, there is a broad service disruption affecting DAFF messaging due to the current Microsoft D365 outage. As a result, clients may not be able to send emails to or receive emails from departmental systems,” the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF) wrote in the notice issued.Microsoft 365 outage: Indigo issues service advisoryIn a post on X, Indigo issued a "Service Advisory" where it said "Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails"."All other support channels remain available. articles.title: From ocean legend to undersea reef: Why has the SS United States been sunk?
articles.summary: The ship had been inactive for years despite various owners attempting to save and restore it.
articles.body:
The historic SS United States ocean liner has taken its final trip, this time to the bottom of the ocean, as it becomes part of an artificial underwater reef .

The nearly 1,000-foot (302m)-long vessel, the fastest ocean liner in the world, was sunk on Wednesday after its hull was hollowed out to ensure it remains on the ocean floor, in a process also known as scuttling.

Over five hours, the ship gradually filled with water and, in its final moments, tilted to its side and sank to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Destin, Florida.

The vessel will now feature as part of the world’s largest artificial reef, which is expected to become a popular diving destination.

Built between 1950 and 1951, the ship was larger than the Titanic, which was 882 feet nine inches (269.1 meters) long. The SS United States was known for its speed, strength and luxury.

Officially launched in 1952, the vessel made history by setting a transatlantic speed record during its first trip, crossing the Atlantic in three days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes at an average speed of 35.59 knots (almost 66km/h). The ocean liner’s record has yet to be broken by another passenger liner.

During 17 years of operation, the SS US carried thousands of passengers, including former Presidents John F Kennedy, Bill Clinton, Harry Truman and Dwight Eisenhower.

Hollywood stars Marilyn Monroe, Elizabeth Taylor and Marlon Brando also graced the ship, as did surrealist painter Salvador Dali and jazz musician Duke Ellington.

With the advent of air travel, the ship’s career came to an end in 1969.

The ship had been inactive for years and remained docked in Philadelphia as various owners attempted to save and restore it.

However, the costs of maintaining the vessel mounted. In 2021, Philadelphia port authorities raised the daily dockage fee to $1,700, which the nonprofit SS United States Conservatory could no longer afford.

In 2024, Florida’s Okaloosa County bought the ship for $1m, with plans to transform it into the world’s largest artificial reef.

According to the county’s website, the ship underwent a yearlong process to ensure it would be environmentally safe to sink as an artificial reef, and the county said it followed all standards set by regulatory agencies.

“Artificial reefs prepared in this way are a benefit to the marine ecosystem, not the other way around. They create habitat that did not previously exist and foster the development of a diverse environment that can thrive for the overall health of the environment that benefits marine life, our fishing industry and tourism as a whole,” a statement from the county says.

The forming of the world’s largest artificial reef is expected to attract wreck divers to the site, creating more tourism opportunities for Florida.

There are an estimated three million shipwrecks lying on sea and ocean floors around the world, according to a 2007 report from the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation.

Many are reclaimed naturally by marine life and are used by coral, eels and snappers as homes.

While some ships are sunk through disaster, others are deliberately sunk to begin reef deployment and attract fish.

Preparation for the sinking of ships is extensive, as harmful substances including paint, wiring and fuel must be removed before they can safely become part of marine life.

Eventually, a sunken ship’s facade will be unrecognisable, with marine life such as fish, barnacles, and crustaceans all inhabiting or using the vessel.

Besides other decommissioned ships which have been deliberately sunk, oil rigs, radio towers and train boxcars have also been used to make artificial reefs on which fish and other marine life can thrive.

More than 600 oil rigs and gas platforms previously installed on the US outer continental shelf were used as part of a 1984 US programme called “Rigs to Reefs” in the Gulf of Mexico.

Other materials have also been used to make artificial reefs, including log huts, household goods such as fridges and shopping trolleys, and even retired New York City subway cars.

Last year, one of the world’s largest artificial reefs was installed around the base of a single wind turbine off the Sussex coast in England. It is made up of 75,000 specifically designed, low-carbon, concrete reef cubes, each with a central chamber and an outer honeycomb texture to encourage marine life to use them.

The cubes were also designed to help the wind farm withstand erosion by acting as a barrier against sea currents and wave energy, slowing sediment that could scour the base.

In Australia, the Queensland Government established its eighth artificial reef in Moreton Bay Marine Park in 2018, using concrete blocks.

Under the official government programme, the first of these reefs expanded the existing Harry Atkison artificial reef, established in 1975 using old car tyres, in 2008 by deploying granite boulders to create new habitats for small fish.

In 2011, the East Coochie Artificial Reef was established using “reef balls” made of hollow concrete; the Wild Banks Artificial Reef was formed by deploying “fish caves”, which are structures made from steel designed to attract more fish species.

In 2011, the South Stradbroke Artificial Reef was also established, and 20 “fish boxes” – cubes with a cross brace made from reinforced concrete – were deployed.

In 2015, the North Moreton Artificial Reef was established in Australia, also using fish boxes. The same year, the Turner Artificial Reef was established, and concrete clusters were deployed.

In 2010, the West Peel Artificial Reef was formed using reef balls.

In 2000, the Mexican government sank two World War II-era decommissioned minesweepers – small warships – and established an artificial reef in the Caribbean marine area.

articles.title: US Senator Chris Van Hollen announces bid to replace Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader
articles.summary: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader, challenging incumbent Democratic leader
articles.body: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader, challenging incumbent Democratic leader Chuck Schumer after the party's victories in the US midterm elections.Van Hollen said on Thursday that he was running because “the American people called for change” and argued that Democrats needed new leadership to respond to the election result.“It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said in a statement. “This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”The leadership election will be held by secret ballot in early December. It is expected to be the first contested election for the position of Democratic leader in decades, with senators privately debating whether Schumer should continue in the role.Schumer has said he has enough support to retain the position. In a statement following Van Hollen’s announcement, he welcomed discussions about the future of the caucus and reiterated that he had the votes to remain its leader.“I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.”Schumer has been speaking to Democratic senators since the election and working on the party's agenda for 2027. During private caucus meetings this week, he outlined a broad plan for the first 100 days of the new majority.“I’m going to win it,” Schumer told the news agency Associated Press in an interview last week.Van Hollen gets support from Sanders, El-SayedVan Hollen has received endorsements from independent Senator Bernie Sanders, who caucuses with Democrats, and Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.Sanders said the election result reflected a demand for a Democratic Party that would challenge powerful special interests and the billionaire class while fighting for working families.“The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats,” Sanders said.El-Sayed had also backed Van Hollen's leadership bid, saying the party needed “bold leadership” after the election.“I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience,” El-Sayed wrote on X. “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.”Sanders and Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan had called for new leadership at a press conference on Tuesday, although neither had then endorsed a specific candidate, AP reported.Several Democratic senators have publicly backed Schumer, including incoming Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Senator Jon Husted in last week's election.Maine Senator Angus King, an independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election, also defended Schumer after Van Hollen's announcement.“Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” King said, adding that Schumer was “one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history”.Disagreement over Schumer's leadershipThe contest follows divisions within the Democratic caucus that became more visible in spring 2025, when Schumer faced criticism after siding with Republicans on a spending vote.Although he subsequently led Democrats through a government shutdown and helped the party's candidates during the midterm campaign, sections of the party's base have continued to call for generational change.Van Hollen, 67, is 75-year-old Schumer's challenger. He has presented himself as a new face for the party and has also said he is considering a presidential run.Speaking to MS NOW, Van Hollen said his decision to contest the leadership position was driven by what he described as a broader demand for change in Washington.“This is not about any one individual, but it is about answering the call of the American people. We saw a huge outburst of democracy on Election Day — red states, blue states, purple states — and it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption and his wars and his cruelty, it was also about a call for a larger change to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favor of the very wealthy against working people, led by a corrupt political system,” he said.Van Hollen also criticised Schumer's involvement in Democratic primaries, accusing him of supporting establishment candidates instead of focusing on defeating Republicans.“We shouldn't have a leader who is getting involved in picking sides in open Democratic primaries, and we should be focused on defeating Republicans. We have two senators right now in the Senate who wouldn't be there if the current majority leader had his way. He supported establishment candidates in the primaries,” he told MS NOW.Van Hollen has also called for action against President Donald Trump over allegations of corruption, supported efforts to impeach defence secretary Pete Hegseth and urged Congress to defund the war in Iran.The December ballot will determine who leads the Senate Democratic caucus as it prepares to take control of the chamber in the next Congress.You use AI every day. articles.title: Microsoft Outlook outage stretches on for hours
articles.summary: The company posted about the disruptions on social media.
articles.body:
A widespread outage involving Microsoft's Outlook email and other applications stretched into Friday morning as the company said it was working to restore service.

The tech giant first posted a statement on social media saying it was "investigating reports of users experiencing issues" accessing online mailboxes shortly before 1 p.m. ET Thursday.

Downdetector , which monitors outages, reported issues with Outlook, Teams and other products on Thursday, as Microsoft attempted to deploy several fixes.

The company has been providing updates on steps to resolve the outage on its Microsoft 365 Status social media account , providing a window into the hourslong effort to troubleshoot the disruption.

In a post shortly after 11:30 p.m. ET , the company said it was working on efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow.

"We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery, so we're reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability," the post stated.

Earlier in the day, the company said: "We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."

Around 6 p.m. ET Thursday, the company said it was "returning a portion of affected servers to the service, and they remain stable so far," though later updated that the servers "can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic" and was working on a fix for that.

Earlier, Microsoft also reported some users were experiencing issues with Microsoft Teams. The company shortly updated that "mitigative actions have successfully restored service health and functionality."

Amid the outage, New York City's Emergency Management Department warned residents of potential delays in reaching city agencies.

"If you are trying to contact a New York City agency by email or access an online City service that relies on Microsoft systems, you may experience delays or temporary disruptions," NYC Emergency Management said on social media. "These issues may affect the delivery of emails, responses from City agencies, and access to certain online services."

For more urgent requests, the city advised residents to try using an alternative method to contact the agency, and to call 311 for non-emergency city services and 911 for emergencies. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

articles.title: Indonesian woman with alleged Chinese links caught at Sonauli border after failing to speak Hindi
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO
articles.body: LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly. Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Migrants offered help to fake artworks to gain UK 'talent' visas - BBC investigation
articles.summary: Going undercover to expose an elaborate fraud aimed at obtaining fast-track settlement for wealthy migrants.
articles.body:
Companies are offering to help migrants pose as talented artists and tech experts to make fraudulent UK visa applications under a fast-track immigration scheme, the BBC has found.

The UK government's Global Talent visa was launched in 2020 to attract the "brightest and best" scientists and researchers from around the world. It is also open to creative artists.

Following our investigation, the Home Office is now revoking visas issued to two Nigerian men who claimed to be fine art photographers, because it believes they were obtained by deception.

Applicants for Global Talent visas are not interviewed. People granted them need to prove they are exceptionally talented or promising in their field. They can then bring their families to the UK and there is a potentially quick path to permanent residency - in three or five years.

We have discovered that wealthy migrants looking to cheat the system are being offered fake art portfolios which they can pass off as their own work for a large fee.

A consultant from one company in London told our undercover reporter - who was posing as a potential client - that his firm could supply artwork produced in China, as well as arrange exhibitions, media coverage and letters of recommendation.

No clients taking the "fully inclusive" package - costing more than £100,000 - had ever been refused a Global Talent visa, he said.

In the case of the two Nigerian men, our investigation was alerted to apparently faked newspaper articles reviewing their artistic work.

A well-known Nigerian art critic told us her name had been attached to online reviews praising the work of the two seemingly obscure artists.

"There is a real problem whereupon fake articles are being implanted onto newspaper websites using bylines of reputable culture journalists," said Molara Wood.

Another woman we spoke to, who tried to get a talent visa via the tech route from India, told us a company she had used fabricated evidence for her application - including a made-up mentoring award and material falsely suggesting she had been a speaker at an event. Her application was rejected.

The Home Office described the findings of our investigation as "extremely serious" and said the company offering the £100,000 package to our reporter was already under investigation.

A spokesperson said they "will not tolerate anyone cheating the UK immigration system".

They added that the Global Talent route was already under review and "the home secretary will take whatever action is needed to stop it being abused".

'It doesn't matter whether you're an artist'

The man who told us artwork could be created in China for clients said he was from a company called iCareer Consultancy UK, based in Canary Wharf. That is also where its sister company, ADArt Global Ltd, which is registered with the government regulator to offer immigration advice, is based.

Social media posts by iCareer employees pitch Global Talent visas as a route for wealthy Chinese nationals to come to the UK, without the need to speak English.

During a phone call and subsequent meeting with our undercover reporter, who spoke in Mandarin, the iCareer consultant told us:

At least four of his clients had obtained a Global Talent visa this year - and he suggested he currently had 10 people in the process of applying

The company could supply an employee to pose as a client and network at gallery openings - to help build evidence for a visa application

For an extra £28,000 the reporter could win a Chinese art award sponsored by Forbes magazine, also to help bolster an application

iCareer denied selling visa services and claimed the consultant had left its employment before he spoke to the undercover reporter - despite continuing to be listed on the company's website and providing us with a contract with the company's name and contact email address.

We began investigating iCareer after receiving a tip-off about its activities in the aftermath of our first investigation into fraudulent asylum claims , when we exposed how law firms and advisers were helping migrants pretend to be gay to obtain asylum.

The company, founded in 2018, is based in a co-working office and advertises itself as providing job search and careers coaching.

A consultant, who gave his name as Peter, had posted multiple times on the Chinese social media platform Xiaohonshu.

In one post from February this year, he boasted: "It doesn't actually matter whether you're an artist… Our Global Talent visa service in the arts is fully inclusive, with guaranteed approval… We say we can do it even if you aren't an artist, because we include the artworks as well."

In another video, Peter - whose real name is Shilong Guan - said he recommended the Global Talent visa in the arts because every other route to UK settlement had an "extremely high English language requirement".

Included in his posts on another social media platform, under the username "iCareerPeter", were redacted names of people whose applications had been approved, he said.

While we could not clarify Peter's claims, a senior immigration lawyer, Harjap Singh Bhangal, who reviewed all our findings, said helping people pose as artists in this way amounted to a "sophisticated fraud".

The whole purpose "is to attempt to defraud the Home Office and convince them, and an endorser, that I'm a genuine person, a genuine artist," he explained.

Although introduced by the Conservatives, Global Talent visas have been enthusiastically championed by the current Labour government - even as it toughens rules elsewhere to try to reduce net migration.

About 6,600 were granted in 2025, with applications in the arts and culture category nearly doubling between 2023 and 2025.

Applications must be approved by the relevant body, which for arts and culture applications is Arts Council England. It endorsed just under half of the nearly 3,500 applications it received last year.

The only way around this is if applicants have won a major award. In the film and TV sector, for example, the award must be an Oscar, Bafta or Golden Globe in one of the main categories.

Arts Council England told us it took allegations of fraud seriously and investigated where evidence was "suggested to have been misleading or fraudulent".

Peter told our undercover reporter it was not a problem if she had no background in art and could not speak English. He could help her get a visa for artists who show "exceptional promise", he said.

"We would handle the production of all your artworks," he explained, adding it was cheaper to commission artists in China than in the UK.

Our reporter would get up to 15 works and have to pay about 10,000 yuan (£1,120) postage to get the works from Beijing to London.

Fine art options included oil paintings, illustration, sculpture, installation, digital art and photography, he explained.

To help her application, Peter said iCareer would arrange exhibitions and media coverage critiquing the reporter's work. Some information would be backdated to make it look like she had been an artist for some time.

During the call, and a subsequent face-to-face meeting, Peter also outlined how he could help our reporter win a prestigious award for Chinese artists - sponsored by American media company, Forbes.

Being a winner in the Forbes China Future Artists Awards would help her visa application, he said, but the additional fee would be about 250,000 yuan (£28,000). Money would be refunded if she did not win.

The BBC approached Forbes for comment and it confirmed to us that the awards are genuine and that ADArt, iCareer Consultancy's sister company, is a sponsor.

It said the judging process is based on the "high standards of Forbes globally" and handled by the Forbes China editorial team, with assistance from professional judges.

Also as part of the visa deception, our reporter would have to do some "work experience… online or in person", said Peter. The reporter asked how she could do this, given she could not speak English.

This was no problem, he responded - one of his colleagues could do it, and also pose as her at gallery openings, to network on her behalf.

Officials administering the visas "don't look at photographs" said Peter.

The whole process would take at least two years, he explained, meaning her application would not be ready until the end of 2028 or early 2029.

The price for the "fully inclusive" visa service would be 880,000 yuan (about £98,000) paid in three stages - with an additional 20% VAT due if our reporter chose to pay in sterling.

During the call, Peter sent over a contract setting out how iCareer would provide "necessary endorsement materials" for a visa application.

The reporter asked if there was any possibility the application wouldn't pass.

"There's no such possibility," Peter replied. "We keep working for you until we get the result."

He added that the reporter would be refunded if her application failed because of material provided by iCareer.

Immigration lawyer Harjap Singh Bhangal said Peter had sent us "a contract to break the law".

When we called Peter to confront him about the claims he had made to our undercover reporter, he denied he was willing to help people pretend to be artists or have artwork made.

"We are not doing anything wrong or illegal, all of our artists are real artists," he told us.

iCareer, via lawyers, subsequently said that Peter's employment had ended in early October, shortly before he spoke to the undercover reporter - adding that the company strongly denied "offering any visa services whatsoever".

"The meeting described by the BBC was not authorised by iCareer," it said. "We do not endorse the representations or purported services attributed to him."

The company added it had been unaware that Peter and another employee had made social media posts promoting these services and would investigate.

It said that ADArt, which has the same owner as iCareer and was described by Peter to the undercover reporter as another division within the iCareer group, "signs artists and helps them curate exhibitions and develop professional relationships".

Peter continued to be listed as an employee on iCareer's website, and on his own LinkedIn profile, until the company was contacted by the BBC, which iCareer described as an oversight.

Our undercover meeting with him took place in the same Canary Wharf building where iCareer and ADArt are based, a co-working space. He also provided us with an iCareer brochure and sent a contract with a corporate iCareer email contact address.

Immigration lawyer Harjap Singh Bhangal says he has no doubt that some fraudulent claims will get through.

We have learned that the two Nigerian men purporting to be fine art photographers - whose visas have now been revoked because of our investigation - successfully obtained talent visas on the basis of faked evidence.

Their deception first came to light when art critic Molara Wood discovered articles reviewing their work in the Nigerian Tribune - which were under her byline despite the fact she had not written them.

The articles were taken down after she alerted the paper's editors.

The Tribune told us it had identified a "staff member who had posted the articles on our website without authorisation".

It said the employee admitted that "an individual outside the organisation had supplied the articles" but that he had denied being paid for it.

Wood said the criticism attributed to her was of poor quality, as were the artworks.

"It is writing that I would not want associated with me," says Wood. "The images were not worthy of comment."

Other critics have also had the same thing happen to them, she says.

Artists applying for the Global Talent visa have to provide at least two examples of recent press coverage reviewing or profiling their work.

The two men who were supposedly reviewed by Wood - Silva Ndifon and Adanu Emmanuel Okoko - are now thought to be living in the UK.

While one of them does boast an online portfolio, it does not feature the kind of fine-art photography described in the article that Wood did not write. The other appears to have little to connect him to photography, or any other kind of art, beyond the article Wood found.

Neither responded to the BBC's requests for comment. After the Home Office was contacted by the BBC, it is now understood their visas are in the process of being revoked.

If you would like to contact our team about this story you can email on: politicsinvestigations@bbc.co.uk

articles.title: Cat brings extremely rare dead songbird into Brampton home
articles.summary: A woman's cat brought in a dead Siberian rubythroat, scarcely seen in the UK, into her home.
articles.body:
A songbird described as a "national rarity" has been found dead after it was caught by a cat.

A woman said her "heart sank" after her cat brought the dead Siberian rubythroat - a species related to the European robin - into her home in Brampton, Cumbria, on Sunday.

Chris Hind, Cumbria's county recorder for birds, said there had only been 17 accepted records of Siberian rubythroat in Britain between 1975 and 2022 due to it being a "very secretive" bird, making this "an extraordinary scenario".

He said the bird, which would be sent off for scientific research, was "very underweight at 28g" and had likely flown from Siberia.

The woman, who wishes to remain anonymous, said she had "heard the cat flap go" and her heart sank when her cat "brought her a bird and trotted off".

"I saw the bird's distinctive beautiful orange-red feather patch under its beak but I couldn't recognise the species," she said.

The woman said she had "popped it in her freezer amongst lollipops" while she researched what it was. She then contacted RSPB Geltsdale, who called the county recorder.

Hind's role involves helping manage about 250,000 recorded bird sightings in Cumbria every year.

He said the Siberian rubythroat was on a national designated list of very rare birds assessed by a panel on the British Birds Rarities Committee.

Hind said he had submitted the record, but he had "absolutely no doubt that it will be accepted because it is a very distinctive looking bird, with a bright red throat".

"It weighed 28g, which is very underweight because we understand the birds to weigh around 75g," he added.

Josh Jones is the senior editor of Bird Guides, a website logging sightings of rare and unusual birds.

He said the species was "notoriously hard for British birdwatchers to see", with it never having been spotted before in Cumbria.

The bird had likely had a "long journey from the vast wilderness of Siberia", he said, adding it was "absolutely tragic that the beautiful bird has fallen victim to a pet cat".

Jones said the Siberian rubythroat was a "largely brown bird but had a wonderful jewel-like crimson throat and it's also got these very striking white eyebrows and moustachial stripes, so it creates this very distinctive facial pattern".

He said: "At this time of year, Siberian rubythroats should be heading south from their Siberian breeding grounds to spend the winter in South-East Asia, highlighting just how far off course this bird in Cumbria was."

"After such a long journey from the vast wilderness of Siberia, it has perished in the most unfortunate of circumstances," Jones said, urging cat owners to fit warning bells to their collars.

"Such deaths are perfectly avoidable by taking the right steps."

Meanwhile, Hind said: "The interesting thing about this, is that the species are very secretive.

"They live their lives concealed among dense vegetation and so, if this cat hadn't brought it in, it's almost impossible that anyone would either have seen it or identified it."

He said once academics had taken any samples from the bird that they needed for their research, it would be sent to the Tullie museum in Carlisle.
